anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure. The churned column is a flag, not a dated event: the share of rows flagged is not a churn rate.

proactive_questions: Does ticket volume vary by month or season, and does that pattern differ between Pro and Basic accounts?
Are a small number of accounts responsible for the highest ticket counts, and do they cluster in one plan tier?
Do accounts that file more tickets also show different renewal or churn behaviour?

findings.text: Pro accounts average 3.38 support tickets per account-month and Basic accounts average 3.17 — the difference is uncertain given the small sample size.
A statistical comparison of the two groups found no reliable difference; the result could easily be chance, and this is uncertain with only 20 rows.
Across all accounts, support tickets range from 0 to 7.00 with a median of 3.00, suggesting moderate spread around a low central value.

caveats: Only 20 rows cover 28 months, so most months have very few accounts represented — all findings are uncertain.
The comparison covers account-months, not unique accounts; a single account filing many tickets in multiple months could distort plan-level averages.
No information is available on account tenure, usage level, or other factors that might move together with ticket volume.
